abstract: Maintains acoustic transponder interrogation telemetry and high-resolution sonar sensor specifications
system_message:
You are Hydrographic survey geophysicist (GEO). As the Hydrographic survey geophysicist (GEO), you oversee acoustic transponder interrogation telemetry and high-resolution sonar sensor specifications, as well as seafloor magnetometry records for candidate salvage operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains acoustic transponder interrogation telemetry and high-resolution sonar sensor specifications（SONAR）
information_points.content:
GEO-SONAR-2X6：For the Towed synthetic aperture sonar deep-tow transect, bench testing of the primary subsea search sensor suite demonstrates that acoustic beacon telemetry compatibility is true. Factory calibration certificates for target classification at a 150 m slant range establish a sonar range resolution of 25 cm.
GEO-SONAR-XVI：For the Autonomous underwater vehicle side-scan sonar grid search, bench testing of the primary subsea search sensor suite confirms that acoustic beacon telemetry compatibility is true. Factory calibration certificates for target classification at a 150 m slant range verify a sonar range resolution of 10 cm.
GEO-SONAR-MSR：For the Remotely operated vehicle acoustic beacon tracking sweep, bench testing of the primary subsea search sensor suite confirms that acoustic beacon telemetry compatibility is true. Factory calibration certificates for target classification at a 150 m slant range indicate a sonar range resolution of 15 cm.

information_points.title: Seafloor magnetometry（MAGMET）
information_points.content:
GEO-MAGMET-7RV：For the Autonomous underwater vehicle side-scan sonar grid search, sensor calibration logs indicate a magnetometer sample rate of 20 Hz on the towed subsea total-field magnetic anomaly sensor.
GEO-MAGMET-0DS：For the Towed synthetic aperture sonar deep-tow transect, calibration bench tests demonstrate a magnetometer sample rate of 30 Hz for the towed subsea total-field magnetic anomaly sensor.
GEO-MAGMET-BHR：For the Remotely operated vehicle acoustic beacon tracking sweep, calibration records verify a magnetometer sample rate of 10 Hz across the towed subsea total-field magnetic anomaly sensor.
